scope: Corollary 5.11 (Two ends with a reserved height variable) of the manuscript “Renewal and changes of law for critical honeycomb walks” (preprints/Renewal-and-changes-of-law-for-critical-honeycomb-walks-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d179fa55e4b82fed), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 29. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose two bridges start at adjacent prescribed ports and stay disjoint through a fixed positive fraction of the smaller height. Their heights and counts lie in the independent bins above, all bounded by CN2. For every ϵ > 0 their critical mass is at most CϵNϵ F, F = κ2 1κ2 2 K1K2 min(κ1, κ2) . (25) An interval of C(1 + r) allowed heights on node i, measurable outside its reserved group, adds min(1, (1 + r)κ −4/3 i ). In particular this applies to the difference of the final endpoint heights after any two terminal pieces have been fixed up to translation. For one nonempty bridge the factor is κ2 i /Ki, with the same optional concentration test.
